name: csv-to-json-converter
description: A script that reads a CSV file and converts it to a JSON file.

promptLevels.beginner: make a script that converts a CSV file to JSON
promptLevels.intermediate: create a function that reads a CSV file and writes out a JSON file with the same data
promptLevels.advanced: write a function that takes a CSV file path as input, parses the CSV (using the first line as headers), and writes a JSON file with the same base name but .json extension
promptLevels.expert: Write a function that accepts a file path to a CSV file as its parameter. Read the CSV file from disk - the first line contains column headers (comma-separated), and subsequent lines contain data rows. Parse this into an array of objects where each object represents a row, with keys from the headers. Write the resulting JSON array to a new file in the same directory with the same name but a .json extension instead of .csv. For example, if input is "/path/to/data.csv", output should be "/path/to/data.json". {languageSpecific}

languageInstructions.typescript: Use Node.js file system APIs (fs module). Include proper TypeScript type annotations for the function parameter and return type. Handle errors appropriately. Export the function.
languageInstructions.javascript: Use Node.js file system APIs (fs module). Export the function as the default export. Handle file reading/writing synchronously or with async/await.
languageInstructions.javascript-jsdoc: Use Node.js file system APIs (fs module). Include comprehensive JSDoc comments: @param for the file path parameter, @returns for what the function returns (if anything), and @description explaining what the function does. Export the function.

variants.javascript-no-comments: Write a JavaScript script that converts a CSV file to a JSON file. The script should be a function that takes a path to a CSV file as input and writes a JSON file with the same name (but a .json extension) in the same directory. The first line of the CSV should be the headers. The script should not have any comments.

testCases.description: Test with a simple CSV file
testCases.test: const csvToJsonConverter = require('./csv-to-json-converter.js'); csvToJsonConverter(testFile); const jsonFile = testFile.replace('.csv', '.json'); const jsonContent = fs.readFileSync(jsonFile, 'utf-8'); const expectedJson = JSON.stringify([{name: 'john', age: '30'}, {name: 'jane', age: '25'}]); console.assert(jsonContent === expectedJson, 'JSON content should match expected');

performanceBenchmarks.name: parse-small-csv
performanceBenchmarks.setup: const fs = require('fs'); const path = require('path'); const os = require('os'); const testFile = path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'perf-small.csv'); const rows = ['name,age,email']; for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) { rows.push(`user${i},${20+i},user${i}@test.com`); } fs.writeFileSync(testFile, rows.join('\n'));

performanceBenchmarks.name: parse-large-csv
performanceBenchmarks.setup: const fs = require('fs'); const path = require('path'); const os = require('os'); const testFile = path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'perf-large.csv'); const rows = ['name,age,email']; for (let i = 0; i < 1000; i++) { rows.push(`user${i},${20+i},user${i}@test.com`); } fs.writeFileSync(testFile, rows.join('\n'));
